newsitem.title: LATVIA: New Latvian mobile phone firm takes first steps.
newsitem.headline: New Latvian mobile phone firm takes first steps.

text.p: The new mobile phone operator in the Baltic state of Latvia, Baltcom GSM, part-owned by Western Wireless Corp and Metromedia International, took its first step to becoming operational on Friday.
The first call using the system was due to be made today by Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans and the company said in a statement that the full service was due to begin in March 1997.
Baltcom is the second mobile operator in Latvia and competes with Latvijas Mobilais Telefons, part-owned by Swedish Telia.
"We are already technically ready to provide telephone connections in Riga and its surroundings," the company said.

Baltcom plans to take half the market share in five years, representing around 50,000 users. It intends to invest $50 million to create a new GSM network over three years, with total investment planned to reach $100 million in 10 years.
"Our main advantage over the the competition will be a better quality (signal) in Riga and coverage of all the major roads in this country," Julijs Krievs, technical manager of Baltcom, told Reuters.
The group's Latvian partner is called Alina.
The transport ministry has decided to limit the number of GSM mobile network operators in Latvia to two for the coming five years.
